page: Microsoft Azure M176bds_4_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization and the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8473C processors clocked at 4.0 GHz, providing 88 physical cores and 176 vCPUs alongside 105 MB of L3 cache. Hardware acceleration features include AVX-512 and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) instructions for vector and matrix computations. The platform integrates 3,892.0 GB of system memory, delivering 22.11 GB of RAM per core, paired with 8,590 GB of high-speed local solid-state storage. No discrete graphics processors are included in this configuration.

Benchmark results highlight extraordinary parallel execution and memory subsystem throughput. In synthetic multi-core evaluations, the server achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core tests and PassMark CPU metrics, including extended instructions, physics, and cryptographic performance. Memory bandwidth reaches 432.05 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 186.0 GB/sec for large-block writes. Application-level evaluations show exceptional scale, recording 169.15 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and leading scores in synthetic database operations alongside multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 816.52 GB/sec. LLM prompt processing for 70B parameter models reaches 39.78 tokens per second.

With its massive memory capacity and balanced multi-threaded compute density, the M176bds_4_v3 delivers cost efficiency by consolidating enterprise-grade workloads onto a single instance instead of distributing state across multiple smaller nodes. The trade-off is single-core performance that lands in the average range despite high multi-core scaling. The instance is suited for massive relational databases, large in-memory databases like SAP HANA or Redis, large-scale transaction processing, and big data ETL processing requiring substantial memory capacity and local NVMe scratch space.
description: Microsoft Azure M176bds_4_v3 is a high-density, memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 176 dedicated vCPUs (88 physical cores) powered by Intel Xeon 8473C processors clocked at 4.0 GHz with 105 MB of L3 cache, alongside Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 support. Hardware resources include 3,892.0 GB of system memory and 8,590 GB of bundled local SSD storage, without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded compute performance, reaching 432.05 GB/sec in uncached read memory bandwidth and 169.15 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Consolidating massive data structures into memory lowers architectural overhead for large enterprise systems. This instance is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, high-throughput transactional databases, enterprise caching layers, and memory-intensive analytics pipelines.
